absent: Layout and callback contracts of the bus operations table and the device identifier record.
Value of the maximum core count and allocation and lifetime rules for bus numbers and core descriptors.
Full parameter list, return codes and call timing of the board invariants callback.
Behavior of the underlying driver registration routine, matching rules and probe and power transition ordering.
Register access ordering, width and side effect rules for the sized and block I/O helpers and interrupt handling.
SPROM layout and write protocol, GPIO and interrupt domain usage, and power up sequencing beyond the PCI passthrough.
Remainder of the ChipCommon register map beyond the truncated slow clock control section.

findings.text: A private wrapper couples a generic device object with a back pointer to its SSB device. The generic object is the visible registration handle while the stored pointer identifies the owning SSB core.

An SSB core descriptor keeps a cached operations pointer as an optimization, two generic device pointers for the core and for DMA, a pointer to the parent bus, an identifier record, an eight bit core index, an interrupt number, plus opaque per device storage and opaque per device type storage.
A conversion helper accepts a pointer to the embedded generic device and returns the associated SSB device by retrieving the enclosing private wrapper and following its stored back pointer.

Per device private storage is written through one setter and read back through one getter, while a separate getter exposes per device type storage without a setter in these fragments. All three operate on opaque pointers carried by the core descriptor.

A driver descriptor carries a name string, a table of matching identifiers, and callbacks for probe, removal, suspend, resume and shutdown with the documented device and state arguments. It embeds a generic driver object, and a conversion macro recovers the enclosing SSB driver from that embedded object.
Driver registration is exposed as a macro that forwards the caller supplied driver descriptor together with the current module handle to the underlying registration routine.
The host bus type is a four way enumeration distinguishing a native system backplane from backplanes attached through PCI, PCMCIA or SDIO.
Board vendor identifiers equal the following: Broadcom equals 0x14E4, Dell equals 0x1028, and HP equals 0x0E11.

Within the SSB board family the following suffixes map to values stated as suffix equals value: BCM94301CB equals 0x0406; BCM94301MP equals 0x0407; BU4309 equals 0x040A; BCM94309CB equals 0x040B; BCM4309MP equals 0x040C; BU4306 equals 0x0416; BCM94306MP equals 0x0418; BCM4309G equals 0x0421; BCM4306CB equals 0x0417; BCM94306PC equals 0x0425; BCM94306CBSG equals 0x042B; PCSG94306 equals 0x042D; BU4704SD equals 0x042E; BCM94704AGR equals 0x042F; BCM94308MP equals 0x0430; BU4318 equals 0x0447; CB4318 equals 0x0448; MPG4318 equals 0x0449; MP4318 equals 0x044A; SD4318 equals 0x044B; BCM94306P equals 0x044C; BCM94303MP equals 0x044E; BCM94306MPM equals 0x0450; BCM94306MPL equals 0x0453; PC4303 equals 0x0454; BCM94306MPLNA equals 0x0457; BCM94306MPH equals 0x045B; BCM94306PCIV equals 0x045C; BCM94318MPGH equals 0x0463; BU4311 equals 0x0464; BCM94311MC equals 0x0465; BCM94311MCAG equals 0x0466.
Board identifiers equal: BU4321 equals 0x046B; BU4321E equals 0x047C; MP4321 equals 0x046C; CB2_4321 equals 0x046D; CB2_4321_AG equals 0x0066; MC4321 equals 0x046E.

Board identifiers equal: BCM94325DEVBU equals 0x0490; BCM94325BGABU equals 0x0491; BCM94325SDGWB equals 0x0492; BCM94325SDGMDL equals 0x04AA; BCM94325SDGMDL2 equals 0x04C6; BCM94325SDGMDL3 equals 0x04C9; BCM94325SDABGWBA equals 0x04E1.

Board identifiers equal: BCM94322MC equals 0x04A4; BCM94322USB equals 0x04A8 and is described as dual band; BCM94322HM equals 0x04B0; BCM94322USB2D equals 0x04BF and is described as single band discrete front end; BU4312 equals 0x048A; BCM4312MCGSG equals 0x04B5.
Chip package codes equal: large 340 pin 4712 equals 0, small 200 pin 4712 equals 1, medium 225 pin 4712 equals 2.

The bus descriptor starts with an MMIO base pointer and an operations pointer, a currently mapped core pointer, and a union holding either the mapped PCMCIA segment number or the SDIO base window address. It then carries a spin lock for switching, a host type tag, and a union of host handles where only the PCI, PCMCIA or SDIO member matching the tag is valid.

The bus descriptor continues with a quirks bitmask, an optional SPROM mutex when SPROM support is enabled, chip identity and SPROM geometry fields, a fixed array of core descriptors plus a device count, a software bus number, embedded ChipCommon PCI MIPS and EXTif core records, board information plus SPROM contents plus a cardbus slot flag that appear only after early init, optional embedded GPIO lock and watchdog and optional GPIO chip with interrupt domain, and internal bookkeeping with a list node, a powered flag and a power warning counter.
One quirk bit is defined for SDIO attached cards requiring a read after each thirty two bit write, with value one shifted left by zero.

Core and segment switching is serialized by the bus bar lock, which on PCMCIA hosts also guards the whole MMIO path. SPROM updates are guarded by a dedicated mutex when that option is enabled, and embedded GPIO register access is guarded by a dedicated GPIO spin lock.

The active host handle is selected by the bus type tag and other union members must not be used. The mapped core pointer is meaningful only on some host buses and is internal to the bus layer. Board data, SPROM data and the cardbus flag are unavailable during early initialization but are present for registered drivers, and the trailing internal bookkeeping fields must be left untouched.

An initialization record bundles board information, SPROM contents and the cardbus slot flag for early setup. A callback type returns an integer status and accepts at least a bus pointer; the visible fragment truncates the remainder of its parameter list so the full contract is absent.

Sized register accessors for eight, sixteen and thirty two bit reads and writes forward the device, offset and value to the per device operations table, and block transfer helpers forward a buffer, count, offset and register width similarly for bulk reads and writes.
DMA translation uses a mask equal to 0xC0000000 and a shift equal to 30.

Two conditional builds exist for PCI host helpers. In one build unregistration forwards to the PCI core and power state changes forward to the host PCI device only when the bus type is PCI. In the other build both helpers accept the same arguments and perform no action.

ChipCommon identification starts at offset 0x0000 with identifier mask equals 0xFFFF, revision mask equals 0xF0000 with shift equals 16, package mask equals 0xF00000 with shift equals 20, and core count mask equals 0xF000000 with shift equals 24. Capabilities at offset 0x0004 include UART count mask equals 0x3, big endian flag equals 0x4, UART clock select equals 0x18 with internal flavor equals 0x8, UART on GPIO equals 0x20, external bus present equals 0xC0, flash type equals 0x700 with none equals 0 plus ST serial equals 0x100 plus Atmel serial equals 0x200 plus parallel equals 0x700, PLL type equals 0x38000 with encodings none equals 0 and type1 equals 0x10000 and type2 equals 0x20000 and type3 equals 0x30000 and type4 equals 0x8000 and type5 equals 0x18000 and type6 equals 0x28000 and type7 equals 0x38000, power control equals 0x40000, OTP size equals 0x380000 with shift equals 19 and base equals 5, JTAG master equals 0x400000, boot ROM equals 0x800000, 64 bit backplane equals 0x8000000, PMU equals 0x10000000, ECI equals 0x20000000, SPROM present equals 0x40000000.

Control and status continue with core control at 0x0008 including UART clock, sync enable and UART enable bits, built in test at 0x000C, OTP status at 0x0010 with program fail and hardware software and CID protect bits, OTP control at 0x0014 with recovery and program wait fields plus shift and fail and select fields, OTP program at 0x0018 with column and row plus shift and error value read start and busy bits where start and busy share one value, interrupt status at 0x0020 and mask at 0x0024 with GPIO and external and watchdog reset bits, chip control at 0x0028 and status at 0x002C for newer revisions, and JTAG command at 0x0030 with start busy pause plus access and width fields that differ between revision ten and eleven encodings, plus instruction at 0x0034 and data at 0x0038 and control at 0x003C with force clock external enable and enable bits. Selected values include watchdog reset equals 0x80000000, GPIO interrupt equals 0x1, external interrupt equals 0x2, JTAG start and busy equal 0x80000000, pause equals 0x40000000.

Flash and GPIO continue with flash control at 0x0040 where start and busy share one value, address at 0x0044 and data at 0x0048, broadcast address at 0x0050 and data at 0x0054, pull up at 0x0058 and pull down at 0x005C for revision twenty and later, input at 0x0060 output at 0x0064 output enable at 0x0068 control at 0x006C polarity at 0x0070 and interrupt at 0x0074, watchdog at 0x0080, LED timer at 0x0088 with off mask equals 0xFFFF and on mask equals 0xFFFF0000 plus shifts zero and sixteen and output mode at 0x008C, clocks N SB PCI M2 and MIPS at 0x0090 through 0x00A0, divider at 0x00A4 with serial flash OTP JTAG and UART fields, on and reference delays at 0x00B0 and 0x00B4, and slow clock control at 0x00B8 for revisions six through nine with source LPO crystal and PCI encodings plus low power oscillator frequency power down and related control bits. The header guard defines LINUX_SSB_CHIPCO_H_.

Misuse hazards include touching the mapped core pointer outside the bus layer or on hosts where it is invalid, dereferencing a host handle whose union member does not match the bus type, reading board or SPROM data during early initialization, assuming MMIO is safe on PCMCIA without holding the bar lock, and omitting the SDIO read after a thirty two bit write on quirked cards.
